text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co on Thursday said it agreed to develop and market DPPE, a cancer treatment, through a license from the Manitoba Cancer Treatment and Research Foundation and the University of Manitoba, Canada.
In studies conducted at the foundation with prostate or breast cancer patients, DPPE appears to enhance chemotherapy without extra side effects.

Bristol-Myers Squibb said it would assume responsibility for worldwide development and marketing of DPPE, which has demonstrated activity in a Phase II trial as combination therapy in patients with hormonally resistant prostate cancer.

In addition, the National Cancer Institute of Canada is undertaking a Phase II trial with DPPE in combination with doxorubicin in the treatment of patients with metastatic breast cancer, Bristol-Myers said.
Bristol-Myers Squibb said it would provide milestone payments to the foundation and the University of Manitoba, as well as royalty payments after marketing.
Details of the financial terms were not disclosed.
